content: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
author: Seneca
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?

practicalInsight: Pick the most important task on your list and work on it for just fifteen focused minutes without touching your phone.
originalQuote: Non est pauper qui habet pauca, sed qui pauca sibi vult habere.
